policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/471 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 February 2026 amending Regulations (EU) No 1308/2013, (EU) No 251/2014 and (EU) 2021/2115 as regards certain market rules and sectoral support measures in the wine sector and for aromatised wine products and Regulation (EU) 2024/1143 as regards certain labelling rules for spirit drinks
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates market rules, financial support, and labelling standards for the wine, aromatised wine, and spirits sectors. It aims to streamline regulations and clarify product information for consumers across member states.
policies.social_reason: Maintains neutral impact on fundamental social rights, welfare, and public health by focusing primarily on technical agricultural market rules and labeling.
policies.environmental_reason: Focuses on administrative market regulations and labelling rather than environmental protections, emissions cuts, or conservation measures.
policies.economic_reason: Supports economic efficiency by streamlining regulations and clarifying market rules for agricultural producers and beverage manufacturers.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/463 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 February 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1348 as regards the application of the concept of safe third country
policies.summary: This European Union regulation amends existing rules regarding the concept of a "safe third country" in asylum procedures. It alters the legal framework for determining whether asylum seekers can be safely sent back to non-EU countries through which they traveled. The policy impacts how member states process refugee claims and manage migration flows across the bloc.
policies.social_reason: Restricts asylum procedures and potential protections for vulnerable refugees by broadening the application of safe third country concepts.
policies.environmental_reason: The policy focuses entirely on migration and asylum law with no direct bearing on environmental protection or emissions.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes administrative costs on member states to implement adjusted asylum procedures without clear economic growth benefits.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/464 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 February 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1348 as regards the establishment of a list of safe countries of origin at Union level
policies.summary: This regulation creates a standardized European Union list of safe countries of origin for asylum seekers. By establishing common criteria across member states, it aims to streamline and accelerate the processing of asylum claims for individuals arriving from nations deemed generally safe.
policies.social_reason: Restricts individual asylum evaluation procedures by fast-tracking claims from designated safe countries, potentially impacting fair access to protection.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct impact on environmental protection, climate change, or natural resources.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes administrative costs on member states to align national lists with the new EU-wide framework without directly boosting economic growth.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/468 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 February 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2024/792 establishing the Ukraine Facility
policies.summary: This document is a formal EU regulation from early 2026 that amends the existing framework governing financial support for Ukraine. It updates the rules and mechanisms under the Ukraine Facility to ensure continued economic and administrative assistance. Essentially, it adjusts how the European Union delivers aid to help stabilize and rebuild Ukraine.
policies.social_reason: Supports public welfare and institutional stability in a nation facing crisis, indirectly protecting the health and livelihoods of citizens.
policies.environmental_reason: The amendment primarily concerns financial and administrative procedures without directly targeting environmental protection or degradation.
policies.economic_reason: Provides crucial funding and economic stabilization mechanisms to support recovery and market resilience in Ukraine.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/467 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 February 2026 implementing enhanced cooperation on the establishment of the Ukraine Support Loan for 2026 and 2027
policies.summary: This regulation establishes a financial loan mechanism to support Ukraine's government operations and stability through 2026 and 2027. It uses enhanced cooperation among European Union member states to provide necessary economic backing during ongoing conflict. The measure aims to ensure Ukraine can maintain basic public services and national resilience.
policies.social_reason: Supports the fundamental wellbeing, security, and stability of a population facing severe conflict and humanitarian crisis.
policies.environmental_reason: The policy focuses exclusively on financial and macroeconomic assistance without direct environmental impacts.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes significant financial costs and fiscal obligations on participating European Union member states to fund external loans.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/361 of 19 February 2026 amending Regulation (EU) No 582/2011 as regards the emissions type-approval of heavy-duty vehicles with on-board fuel and energy consumption monitoring devices
policies.summary: This regulation updates EU rules for heavy-duty vehicles, such as trucks and buses, to ensure their on-board fuel and energy consumption monitoring devices function correctly. By improving how vehicle emissions and fuel use are tracked during real-world driving, it helps ensure that official environmental standards are actually being met. Ultimately, this transparency supports Europe's broader climate goals by keeping manufacturers accountable for real-world pollution.
policies.social_reason: Improves public health by ensuring accurate monitoring of heavy vehicle emissions, reducing air pollution in communities.
policies.environmental_reason: Enhances the enforcement of environmental standards for heavy-duty vehicles, leading to better tracking and potential reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes minimal administrative updates on manufacturers for type-approval while creating a more transparent and standardized market for fuel-efficient technologies.

policies.title: UN Regulation No. 12 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to the protection of the driver against the steering mechanism in the event of impact [2026/300]
policies.summary: This regulation sets mandatory safety standards for vehicle steering mechanisms to protect drivers from serious injury during a frontal collision. It requires manufacturers to design steering columns and wheels that absorb impact energy rather than thrusting rigidly into the driver. Ultimately, this international standard ensures that cars sold in participating regions meet rigorous crash-protection criteria.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to safer vehicles by mandating engineering standards that directly reduce driver fatalities and severe chest or head injuries during crashes.
policies.environmental_reason: Neutral because the regulation focuses exclusively on occupant physical safety rather than vehicle emissions, fuel efficiency, or environmental conservation.
policies.economic_reason: Promotes economic stability and fair trade by standardizing safety requirements across international markets, preventing fragmented regulations while adding only modest compliance costs for manufacturers.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/384 of 17 February 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 314/2004 concerning restrictive measures in view of the situation in Zimbabwe
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates and modifies existing restrictive measures, such as sanctions, regarding the political situation in Zimbabwe. It alters how the EU applies financial or travel restrictions in response to governance and human rights concerns in the country.
policies.social_reason: Supports human rights and democratic governance by maintaining targeted international pressure against abuses.
policies.environmental_reason: The policy focuses entirely on geopolitical sanctions and has no direct impact on environmental protection or emissions.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes targeted trade and financial restrictions that create minor compliance costs and friction for international commerce.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/340 of 16 February 2026 correcting certain language versions of Regulation (EU) No 231/2012 laying down specifications for food additives listed in Annexes II and III to Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council
policies.summary: This regulation fixes translation and wording errors in different language versions of previously established European Union rules regarding food additive specifications. It ensures that food safety standards and descriptions are accurately and consistently understood across all member states. The policy does not change existing health rules or introduce new requirements for citizens or businesses.
policies.social_reason: Maintains the status quo by merely correcting translation errors without altering public health or consumer rights.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct impact on environmental protection, pollution, or natural resources.
policies.economic_reason: Brings negligible administrative clarity with no broader economic impact on markets or employment.

policies.title: UN Regulation No 167 – Uniform Provisions concerning the approval of motor vehicles with regard to their Direct Vision [2026/272]
policies.summary: This regulation sets new safety standards for motor vehicle design to ensure drivers have a better direct line of sight. By improving visibility around large vehicles, it aims to protect vulnerable road users like pedestrians and cyclists from blind-spot accidents.
policies.social_reason: Enhances public safety and protects vulnerable road users by mandating better vehicle design to prevent fatal collisions.
policies.environmental_reason: Directly focuses on vehicle safety design rather than environmental emissions or habitat conservation.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes compliance and re-engineering costs on vehicle manufacturers, which may be passed on to consumers.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/338 of 13 February 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1803 as regards International Financial Reporting Standard 18
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates financial reporting rules by incorporating International Financial Reporting Standard 18 into European law. It aims to improve how companies present their financial performance, making it easier for investors and the public to understand corporate accounts. Ultimately, it standardizes business transparency across the bloc without changing fundamental tax or spending policies.
policies.social_reason: Enhances corporate transparency, helping everyday investors and stakeholders make more informed financial decisions.
policies.environmental_reason: This regulation deals strictly with corporate financial accounting standards and has no direct environmental impact.
policies.economic_reason: Improves market efficiency and comparability by streamlining international financial reporting standards for businesses.

policies.title: Canada Gazette - Part II, February 11, 2026, volume 159, number 3
policies.summary: This document is the official publication notice for the Canada Gazette Part II, which releases government regulations, statutory instruments, and official notices bi-weekly. It serves an administrative and transparency function for the Canadian government without introducing new substantive policy changes on its own.
policies.social_reason: Maintains government transparency and administrative publication schedules without directly affecting citizens' rights or welfare.
policies.environmental_reason: Serves a routine administrative function with no direct impact on environmental protection or pollution.
policies.economic_reason: Acts as a standard administrative publication with no direct impact on markets, jobs, or economic growth.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382 of 11 February 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 1186/2009 as regards the elimination of the threshold-based customs duty relief
policies.summary: This EU regulation removes the customs duty exemption for low-value packages imported from outside the bloc. As a result, shoppers and e-commerce platforms will now have to pay import duties on all items, regardless of how cheap they are. The change aims to protect local businesses from unfair competition and close loopholes exploited by cheap foreign goods.
policies.social_reason: Increases the cost of everyday consumer goods for lower-income households who frequently purchase inexpensive items online.
policies.environmental_reason: Reduces the incentive for ordering massive quantities of cheap, disposable goods shipped individually from overseas, potentially cutting transport emissions.
policies.economic_reason: Levels the playing field for domestic European retailers and manufacturers by removing the unfair tax advantage previously enjoyed by ultra-cheap foreign e-commerce platforms.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/405 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 February 2026 on detergents and surfactants, and repealing Regulation (EC) No 648/2004 (Text with EEA relevance)
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates rules on detergents and surfactants to better protect the environment and public health from harmful chemical substances. It streamlines market requirements for manufacturers while ensuring safer cleaning products are sold across member states.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by reducing exposure to potentially harmful chemical substances found in common household cleaners.
policies.environmental_reason: Improves environmental safety by establishing stricter biodegradability standards and controls for surfactants and detergents entering ecosystems.
policies.economic_reason: Streamlines regulatory compliance and creates a level playing field for detergent manufacturers operating within the European market.

policies.title: Commission Directive (EU) 2026/288 of 9 February 2026 amending Council Directive 91/676/EEC as regards the use of certain fertilising materials from livestock manure
policies.summary: This EU directive updates rules on how farmers can use processed fertilizers made from livestock manure. It aims to modernize agricultural practices while managing nutrient runoff and soil health across member states.
policies.social_reason: Supports public health and rural communities by setting safer standards for agricultural fertilizer use.
policies.environmental_reason: Reduces the risk of water pollution and environmental degradation by regulating the application of manure-based fertilizers.
policies.economic_reason: Provides farmers with clearer regulatory guidance for utilizing organic fertilizers, potentially lowering input costs.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/250 of 2 February 2026 correcting Regulation (EU) 2024/3190 on the use of bisphenol A (BPA) and other bisphenols and bisphenol derivatives with harmonised classification for specific hazardous properties in certain materials and articles intended to come into contact with food, amending Regulation (EU) No 10/2011 and repealing Regulation (EU) 2018/213
policies.summary: This EU regulation corrects a previous law regarding the use of harmful bisphenol chemicals, such as BPA, in materials that come into contact with food. It ensures that restrictions and safety rules protecting consumers from toxic chemical exposure are accurately applied and enforced. The update helps close regulatory loopholes to better safeguard public health and food safety standards.
policies.social_reason: Expands public health protections by ensuring strict and accurate legal limits on hazardous chemicals in food packaging.
policies.environmental_reason: Reduces the release of toxic synthetic chemicals into the environment and food chain through stricter regulatory controls.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes minor compliance adjustments for manufacturers while creating a clearer, more predictable regulatory standard for the food packaging industry.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/247 of 2 February 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 300/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards specifications for national quality control programmes in the field of civil aviation security
policies.summary: This regulation updates European Union rules to improve how national governments test and check airport security measures. It aims to ensure that aviation security standards remain high and consistent across member countries. For everyday travelers, it simply means behind-the-scenes security checks are managed under stricter, updated guidelines.
policies.social_reason: Enhances public safety by ensuring more rigorous security oversight at airports.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct impact on environmental protection, emissions, or natural habitats.
policies.economic_reason: Involves administrative adjustments to government oversight with minimal direct impact on broader economic growth or consumer costs.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/245 of 2 February 2026 amending Annex I to Regulation (EU) No 10/2011 as regards the authorisation or the conditions of use of several substances
policies.summary: This regulation updates European Union safety rules regarding the chemical substances permitted in plastic materials that come into contact with food. It specifically revises which substances are authorized and the conditions under which they can be safely used. These updates help protect public health by ensuring that harmful chemicals do not leach into what people eat.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by strengthening safety standards for materials that come into contact with everyday food.
policies.environmental_reason: Supports better chemical management and safety controls that indirectly reduce harmful chemical persistence in products.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes minor regulatory compliance costs on manufacturers while ensuring fair standards across the single market.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/271 of 29 January 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1529 concerning restrictive measures in view of Iran’s military support to Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and to armed groups and entities in the Middle East and the Red Sea region
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates and tightens economic sanctions against Iran in response to its military support for Russia's war in Ukraine and destabilizing activities in the Middle East. It imposes additional asset freezes and travel bans on individuals and entities involved in supplying weapons and military technology.
policies.social_reason: Supports international security and human rights indirectly by penalizing the proliferation of weapons used in aggressive conflicts.
policies.environmental_reason: This policy focuses on geopolitical sanctions and has no direct impact on environmental protection or pollution.
policies.economic_reason: Restricts international trade and financial transactions with designated Iranian entities, causing minor friction for global commerce.

policies.title: UN Regulation No. 107 - Uniform provisions concerning the approval of category M2 or M3 vehicles with regard to their general construction [2026/139]
policies.summary: This international regulation sets uniform safety and construction standards for large passenger vehicles like buses and coaches. It ensures that manufacturers build these vehicles to safely transport passengers, including provisions for general safety and structural integrity.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to safer public transportation by mandating rigorous construction standards that protect passengers.
policies.environmental_reason: Supports efficiency indirectly through modern vehicle design standards, though its primary focus is safety rather than emissions.
policies.economic_reason: Promotes fair trade and market harmonization by creating a single set of vehicle construction standards across participating nations.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/215 of 29 January 2026 amending Annexes II and V to Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards maximum residue levels for dimoxystrobin, ethephon and propamocarb in or on certain products
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates the maximum permitted levels of certain agricultural chemicals—dimoxystrobin, ethephon, and propamocarb—that can remain on food products. It aims to protect public health by setting strict safety standards for chemical residues in what people eat. These adjustments ensure that agricultural practices align with the latest scientific health data.

policies.environmental_reason: Protects ecosystems and biodiversity by strictly regulating the use and safe thresholds of potentially harmful agricultural chemicals.
policies.economic_reason: Balances compliance costs for farmers with the necessary public health standards, resulting in a neutral overall economic impact.

policies.title: Canada Gazette - Part II, January 28, 2026, volume 159, number 2

policies.social_reason: Maintains neutral administrative transparency without directly affecting citizen rights, welfare, or health.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct impact on environmental protection or pollution levels.
policies.economic_reason: Serves a purely informational and administrative function with no direct impact on economic growth, jobs, or market costs.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/196 of 28 January 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the use of carrageenan (E 407), locust bean gum (E 410), guar gum (E 412), gum arabic (acacia gum) (E 414), xanthan gum (E 415), pectins (E 440) and starch sodium octenyl succinate (E 1450) and Commission Regulation (EU) No 231/2012 as regards specifications for locust bean gum (E 410), guar gum (E 412), gum arabic (acacia gum) (E 414), xanthan gum (E 415), pectins (E 440) and starch sodium octenyl succinate (E 1450)
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates safety and purity standards for several common food additives, including various gums, pectins, and starches used to thicken and stabilize foods. It amends existing rules to ensure these substances meet the latest scientific safety evaluations and technical specifications. These changes help protect consumer health while giving food manufacturers clear guidelines on ingredient quality.

policies.environmental_reason: Has a negligible direct impact on environmental protection or natural habitats.
policies.economic_reason: Provides regulatory clarity and harmonization for food producers operating within the EU market.

policies.title: Commission Directive (EU) 2026/192 of 28 January 2026 amending Appendix A of Annex II to Directive 2009/48/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety of toys, as regards cobalt
policies.summary: This EU directive updates safety standards for children's toys by introducing stricter limits on the presence of the chemical element cobalt. It aims to protect young children from potential health risks associated with toxic substance exposure during play. Toy manufacturers will need to ensure their products comply with these lower permissible levels of cobalt.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by reducing children's exposure to potentially toxic chemicals in toys.
policies.environmental_reason: Indirectly promotes safer manufacturing practices and reduces hazardous material waste.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes minor compliance and testing costs on toy manufacturers and importers.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/189 of 28 January 2026 amending Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and the Council and Commission Regulation (EU) No 231/2012 as regards the use of shellac (E 904) in food for special medical purposes in tablet and coated tablet forms
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates food additive rules to permit the use of shellac, a common glazing agent, in specific medical foods presented as tablets. It ensures that patients requiring specialized medical nutrition have better access to safe, coated oral formulations. The update aligns food additive specifications with modern manufacturing needs for medical products.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to better-formulated medical foods, slightly improving convenience and adherence for patients relying on specialized nutrition.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no significant direct impact on environmental protection or pollution.
policies.economic_reason: Supports the medical food manufacturing industry by standardizing regulatory requirements for tablet coatings.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/261 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 January 2026 on phasing out Russian natural gas imports and preparing the phase-out of Russian oil imports, improving monitoring of potential energy dependencies and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/1938
policies.summary: This European Union regulation implements a complete phase-out of Russian natural gas and lays the groundwork for eliminating Russian oil imports. It enhances monitoring mechanisms to track and prevent dangerous energy dependencies on external suppliers, strengthening the bloc's energy security.
policies.social_reason: Protects citizens from sudden energy shortages and geopolitical coercion, though short-term market adjustments could temporarily impact household utility costs.
policies.environmental_reason: Accelerates the transition away from fossil fuels by forcing a permanent break from Russian hydrocarbons and reducing overall dependency on high-emission energy sources.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes short-term economic friction and adjustment costs on industries heavily reliant on traditional supply chains, despite long-term strategic resilience.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/175 of 26 January 2026 amending Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1334/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the inclusion of hesperetin dihydrochalcone in the Union list of flavourings
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates the official list of approved food flavorings to include hesperetin dihydrochalcone. Food manufacturers can now legally use this specific substance to add taste to their products across the European Union.
policies.social_reason: Maintains neutral impact on public rights and health as it merely regulates a routine food additive following safety checks.
policies.environmental_reason: Maintains neutral impact on the environment with no direct bearing on emissions, habitats, or natural resources.
policies.economic_reason: Supports economic activity by providing food businesses with regulatory clarity and a new approved ingredient option.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/172 of 26 January 2026 amending Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 1334/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the inclusion of 3-[3-(2-isopropyl-5-methyl-cyclohexyl)-ureido]-butyric acid ethyl ester in the Union list of flavourings and correcting certain CAS numbers
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates the official list of approved food flavourings by adding a specific chemical compound used to modify tastes. policies.summary: This European Union regulation sets catch limits and fishing opportunities for various fish stocks in EU and certain non-EU waters for the years 2026, 2027, and 2028. It aims to balance the economic needs of the fishing industry with the long-term sustainability of marine ecosystems. The policy updates previous rules to reflect scientific advice on fish population health.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/266 of 26 January 2026 fixing for 2026 the fishing opportunities for certain fish stocks and groups of fish stocks applicable in the Mediterranean and Black Seas
policies.summary: This European Union regulation sets annual fishing limits and quotas for specific fish stocks in the Mediterranean and Black Seas for the year 2026. Its goal is to manage marine resources to ensure fish populations remain at sustainable levels while supporting the fishing industry. By controlling catch limits, the policy aims to prevent overfishing and protect marine biodiversity in these regions.
policies.social_reason: Sustains long-term coastal community livelihoods and food security through responsible management.
policies.environmental_reason: Protects marine ecosystems and aids fish stock recovery by establishing legally binding catch limits.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/176 of 26 January 2026 amending Regulation (EU) No 142/2011 as regards transitional measures for export of meat-and-bone meal as a fuel for combustion
policies.summary: This regulation extends temporary rules allowing the export of meat-and-bone meal to be used as fuel for combustion in specific third countries. It updates existing European animal byproduct frameworks to facilitate alternative fuel usage while maintaining regulatory oversight. The measure primarily affects agricultural and waste-to-energy logistics rather than everyday citizens.
policies.social_reason: Neutral impact on everyday citizens as this is a technical trade and waste management adjustment.
policies.environmental_reason: Permits the combustion of animal byproducts for energy, which can involve carbon emissions and air pollution associated with burning organic waste.
policies.economic_reason: Provides a modest economic benefit to agricultural producers and waste processors by enabling an alternative market and disposal method for meat-and-bone meal.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/140 of 22 January 2026 amending Annexes II and III to Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards maximum residue levels for acequinocyl, chlormequat, metalaxyl-M, pyraclostrobin, sulfoxaflor and trifloxystrobin in or on certain products
policies.summary: This regulation updates the European Union's safety limits for specific pesticide residues found on or in food and agricultural products. It adjusts the maximum allowed amounts based on the latest scientific assessments to ensure food safety for consumers. These changes apply uniformly across member states to protect public health while regulating agricultural trade.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by updating and tightening safety limits for hazardous pesticide residues on food products.
policies.environmental_reason: Reduces environmental toxicity by carefully monitoring and restricting chemical residue levels associated with certain agricultural pesticides.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes minor compliance adjustments on agricultural producers with a negligible overall impact on broader economic growth.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2026/147 of 22 January 2026 amending Annexes II and V to Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards maximum residue levels for benfluralin, benthiavalicarb and penflufen in or on certain products
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates the maximum permitted levels of specific chemical pesticide residues allowed in or on certain food and feed products. It ensures that agricultural practices remain compliant with safety standards designed to protect consumers from chemical exposure. policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/211 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 January 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1755 as regards the amounts allocated to Member States under the Brexit Adjustment Reserve
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates how financial aid from the Brexit Adjustment Reserve is distributed among member countries. It adjusts the allocated funding amounts to help nations better manage the economic and financial impacts caused by the United Kingdom leaving the European Union.

policies.title: P10_TA(2026)0001 – Framework for strengthening the availability and security of supply of critical medicinal products as well as the availability of, and accessibility of, medicinal products of common interest – Amendments adopted by the European Parliament on 20 January 2026 on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council laying a framework for strengthening the availability and security of supply of critical medicinal products as well as the availability of, and accessibility of, medicinal products of common interest, and amending Regulation (EU) 2024/795 (COM(2025)0102 – C10-0048/2025 – 2025/0102(COD)) (Ordinary legislative procedure: first reading)
policies.summary: This European Parliament legislative proposal aims to secure and strengthen the supply and availability of critical medicines across member states. policies.economic_reason: Boosts economic resilience and public-interest market stability by preventing costly medical supply disruptions and coordinating pharmaceutical manufacturing within the bloc.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/150 of 16 January 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1173 on establishing the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
policies.summary: This regulation updates the rules for the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking, a cooperative effort to build world-class supercomputing infrastructure across Europe. policies.title: UN Regulation No. 80 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of seats of large passenger vehicles and of these vehicles with regard to the strength of the seats and their anchorages [2026/54]
policies.summary: This international regulation sets strict safety standards for the strength of seats and their anchorages in large passenger buses and coaches. It ensures that seats are built to withstand high impact forces, ultimately protecting passengers during collisions. policies.economic_reason: Promotes a level playing field and maritime commerce efficiency by harmonizing safety and regulatory standards across the EU.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2518 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 laying down additional procedural rules on the enforcement of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (Text with EEA relevance)
policies.summary: This EU regulation establishes clearer and more efficient procedural rules for enforcing the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) across member states. It streamlines how cross-border privacy complaints are handled, making it easier for data protection authorities to cooperate and hold companies accountable. Ultimately, this helps ensure that citizens' digital privacy rights are applied consistently and swiftly throughout the European Union.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to justice and strengthens data privacy protections for citizens facing cross-border violations.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct impact on environmental protection or natural resources.
policies.economic_reason: Improves regulatory clarity and reduces compliance friction for businesses operating across multiple EU borders.

policies.title: Directive (EU) 2025/2456 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 amending Directive 2011/65/EU as regards the reattribution of scientific and technical tasks to the European Chemicals Agency (Text with EEA relevance)
policies.summary: This European Union directive officially transfers specific scientific and technical responsibilities regarding hazardous substances in electrical equipment from the European Commission to the European Chemicals Agency. By streamlining how these chemical regulations are managed, the policy ensures that specialized agency experts handle safety evaluations and compliance tasks efficiently. This administrative shift does not change existing environmental or safety rules, but rather improves how they are technically administered.
policies.social_reason: Supports public health and safety by ensuring expert administrative oversight of hazardous materials in consumer electronics.
policies.environmental_reason: Enhances the technical execution of environmental regulations governing restricted substances in electrical and electronic equipment.
policies.economic_reason: Constitutes an internal administrative reallocation of duties with negligible direct impact on broader economic markets or costs.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2458 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 on European statistics on population and housing, amending Regulation (EC) No 862/2007 and repealing Regulations (EC) No 763/2008 and (EU) No 1260/2013 (Text with EEA relevance)
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates and standardizes how member countries collect, process, and share population and housing statistics. It aims to make demographic data more comparable, timely, and accessible across the European Union. By modernizing these data systems, it helps policymakers better understand housing needs and population trends.
policies.social_reason: Improves evidence-based policymaking for housing, healthcare, and social services by providing more accurate demographic data.
policies.environmental_reason: Directly impacts neither environmental protection nor degradation, though better housing data could indirectly inform urban planning.
policies.economic_reason: Streamlines administrative reporting processes for member states, leading to minor long-term efficiency gains in public sector resource allocation.

policies.title: Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2025/2445 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 on the statute and funding of European political parties and European political foundations (recast)
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates the rules on how European political parties and foundations are funded and operated. It aims to make political funding more transparent, ensure compliance with EU values, and prevent misuse of public money. The updated statute also clarifies administrative requirements for these pan-European political organizations.
policies.social_reason: Expands democratic accountability and transparency by ensuring European political parties uphold EU values and properly manage public funds.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct or significant impact on environmental protection, emissions, or natural habitats.
policies.economic_reason: Improves financial oversight and regulatory clarity for the allocation of public funds to European political entities.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2455 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 establishing a common data platform on chemicals, laying down rules to ensure that the data contained in it are findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable and establishing a monitoring and outlook framework for chemicals (Text with EEA relevance)
policies.summary: This European Union regulation establishes a centralized digital platform to collect and share data about various chemicals. It aims to make chemical safety information easily accessible to the public and authorities while setting up a monitoring framework to track chemical trends and future challenges.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to public safety information by creating a transparent, interoperable database that helps protect health and consumer rights.
policies.environmental_reason: Enhances environmental protection by providing better data monitoring and outlook frameworks to track hazardous chemicals and pollution.
policies.economic_reason: Streamlines regulatory compliance and data sharing for businesses, though it may introduce some initial administrative adaptation costs.

policies.title: Directive (EU) 2025/2459 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 amending Directive 1999/62/EC as regards the extension of the period in which zero-emission heavy-duty vehicles can benefit from significantly reduced rates of infrastructure or user charges or from exemptions to pay them (Text with EEA relevance)
policies.summary: This European Union directive extends financial incentives, such as reduced road tolls or exemptions, for zero-emission heavy-duty trucks like electric or hydrogen lorries. The goal is to encourage transport companies to upgrade their fleets to cleaner vehicles by lowering their operating costs. This helps accelerate the transition toward green logistics across Europe.
policies.social_reason: Improves public health by reducing harmful diesel emissions and air pollution along major freight corridors.
policies.environmental_reason: Accelerates the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and pollution by incentivizing zero-emission heavy-duty transport.
policies.economic_reason: Lowers operational costs for early-adopting freight companies, though it may temporarily shift road infrastructure maintenance funding burdens.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2439 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 November 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2024/2865 as regards dates of application and transitional provisions (Text with EEA relevance)
policies.summary: This EU regulation simply delays the enforcement dates and transitional periods for a previously agreed-upon set of rules. It gives businesses and governments more time to prepare and comply without changing the actual substance of the underlying laws.
policies.social_reason: Maintains the status quo by merely adjusting timelines rather than altering rights, welfare, or health provisions.
policies.environmental_reason: Delays administrative deadlines without altering the underlying environmental standards or protection measures.
policies.economic_reason: Reduces immediate compliance costs and administrative burdens for businesses by providing a longer transition period.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/2397 of 24 November 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2016/1686 imposing additional restrictive measures directed against ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaeda and natural and legal persons, entities or bodies associated with them
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates and extends financial and travel sanctions targeting individuals and groups linked to terrorist organizations like ISIL and Al-Qaeda. It aims to prevent these actors from accessing funds and economic resources within EU member states. By maintaining and updating these restrictive measures, the EU seeks to bolster international security and counter terrorist financing.
policies.social_reason: Expands public safety by maintaining targeted restrictive measures against individuals and entities associated with terrorist networks.
policies.environmental_reason: Directs security measures against terrorist financing with negligible impact on the environment.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes targeted asset freezes on specific individuals and entities without causing broader systemic economic effects.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/2627 of 17 November 2025 on the allocation of the fishing opportunities provided for in the Protocol on the implementation of the Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the European Union and the Government of the Cook Islands (2025-2032)
policies.summary: This EU regulation allocates fishing quotas and opportunities in Cook Islands waters for European vessels under a specific sustainable fisheries agreement. It sets the legal framework for EU fleets to operate in these Pacific waters while managing catch limits through 2032. The measure essentially coordinates international commercial fishing access between the EU and the Cook Islands.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2342 of 13 November 2025 establishing a fisheries closure for redfish in international waters of 1 and 2 for vessels flying the flag of or registered in a Member State of the European Union
policies.summary: This European Union regulation temporarily bans fishing for redfish in specific international waters because catch limits have been reached. It applies to all EU-flagged vessels to prevent overfishing and protect the fish population. The closure remains in effect until the end of the year.
policies.social_reason: Protects long-term food security and coastal livelihoods by preventing the collapse of a key fish stock.
policies.environmental_reason: Safeguards marine biodiversity and prevents overexploitation of redfish populations in international waters.
policies.economic_reason: Causes short-term economic losses for commercial fishing operators by halting their harvesting activities in this region.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2365 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 November 2025 on preventing plastic pellet losses to reduce microplastic pollution
policies.summary: This European Union regulation aims to prevent the accidental loss of plastic pellets during handling and transport to reduce microplastic pollution in the environment. It requires companies that handle plastic pellets to implement strict risk management plans, containment measures, and employee training. Ultimately, the policy protects ecosystems and human health from the accumulation of hazardous plastic particles in nature and the food chain.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by reducing the intake of harmful microplastics through the environment and food chain.
policies.environmental_reason: Significantly curbs microplastic pollution and safeguards aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems from plastic pellet contamination.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes initial compliance costs on businesses handling plastic pellets, balanced by long-term environmental and health savings.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2269 of 12 November 2025 correcting Regulation (EU) 2022/1616 as regards labelling of recycled plastic, the development of recycling technologies and the transfer of authorisations
policies.summary: This EU regulation makes technical corrections to existing rules about recycled plastics. It updates labeling requirements, supports the development of new recycling technologies, and clarifies how recycling authorizations can be transferred between companies.
policies.social_reason: Expands consumer transparency through improved labeling of recycled plastic products.
policies.environmental_reason: Supports the development and implementation of advanced plastic recycling technologies.
policies.economic_reason: Reduces administrative burdens and regulatory friction for recycling businesses through clearer authorization rules.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2274 of 12 November 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1487 as regards the adoption of the work programme for the gradual review of safeners and synergists
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates the schedule for a thorough safety review of certain chemical additives used in pesticides, known as safeners and synergists. It ensures these substances are systematically evaluated to determine if they pose risks to human health or the environment before they can remain on the market. Ultimately, the measure helps regulatory bodies manage agricultural chemicals more effectively to protect public safety.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by ensuring chemical additives in pesticides undergo rigorous safety evaluations.
policies.environmental_reason: Reduces potential ecological harm by systematically reviewing chemical substances used in agriculture.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes standard administrative regulatory processes with negligible direct impact on broader economic growth.

policies.title: Directive (EU) 2025/2360 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 November 2025 on soil monitoring and resilience (Soil Monitoring Law)
policies.summary: This EU directive establishes a comprehensive framework for monitoring and assessing soil health across member states to ensure sustainable land management. It requires countries to address contaminated sites, combat desertification, and improve overall soil resilience to protect ecosystems and human health. Ultimately, the law aims to achieve healthy soils throughout the Union by 2050.
policies.social_reason: Improves public health and living conditions by identifying and cleaning up harmful soil contamination in populated areas.
policies.environmental_reason: Dramatically enhances biodiversity, combats desertification, and protects vital ecosystems through mandatory soil health monitoring and restoration.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes initial compliance and remediation costs on landowners and businesses, but yields long-term economic benefits by preserving agricultural productivity.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2262 of 11 November 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/826 to clarify definitions and some aspects of the measurement conditions and amending Regulation (EU) 2023/2533 in relation to the methodology for calculating the average final moisture content, the identification and availability of spare parts and of repair information among other aspects
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates technical rules for electronic appliances regarding energy efficiency and eco-design standards. It clarifies definitions, measurement conditions, and rules on the availability of spare parts and repair information to help products last longer. Ultimately, it ensures that manufacturers make it easier to fix household electronics while standardizing how energy use is measured.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to repair information and spare parts, making it easier and cheaper for everyday consumers to fix their appliances.
policies.environmental_reason: Reduces electronic waste and resource consumption by encouraging product repair and improving the enforcement of eco-design standards.
policies.economic_reason: Generates minor economic benefits for consumers through lower repair costs, though it imposes technical compliance adjustments on manufacturers.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2306 of 7 November 2025 establishing a fisheries closure for small-eyed ray in area 7e for vessels flying the flag of France
policies.summary: This regulation temporarily bans French fishing vessels from catching small-eyed ray in a specific area (zone 7e) because the catch limit has been reached. It is a routine fisheries management measure designed to prevent overfishing of this particular ray species. For the general public, it has no direct everyday impact, though it affects commercial fishermen operating in that region.
policies.social_reason: Neutral impact on public social welfare, affecting only a specific commercial fishing sector rather than broader rights or health.
policies.environmental_reason: Protects marine ecosystems by enforcing fishing quotas to prevent the depletion of small-eyed ray populations.
policies.economic_reason: Restricts commercial fishing operations for French vessels in the specified zone, causing temporary revenue loss for those affected.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2311 of 7 November 2025 establishing a fisheries closure for European hake in GFCM geographical subareas 8, 9, 10 and 11 for vessels flying the flag of France
policies.summary: This European Union regulation temporarily stops French fishing vessels from catching European hake in specific Mediterranean areas to protect depleted fish populations. The measure is designed to allow fish stocks to recover and ensure long-term sustainability in the region's marine ecosystem. While aimed at ecological preservation, it will temporarily halt fishing operations for the affected commercial fleets.
policies.social_reason: Restricts the livelihood and daily working activities of fishers in the short term, though it aims to secure future food supplies.
policies.environmental_reason: Protects vulnerable marine species from overfishing and promotes the recovery of depleted fish stocks in the Mediterranean.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes immediate economic costs and revenue losses on commercial fishing operations by halting targeted harvesting.

policies.social_reason: Maintains standard administrative transparency without directly altering social rights, welfare, or public services.

policies.economic_reason: Has no direct impact on economic growth, employment, or financial markets.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2225 of 5 November 2025 amending Annex II to Directive 2002/46/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards magnesium L-threonate as a source of magnesium used in the manufacture of food supplements
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates food supplement rules to officially allow magnesium L-threonate as a legal source of magnesium in the manufacturing process. It ensures that this specific chemical form meets safety standards so it can be used safely in dietary products sold across Europe.
policies.social_reason: Expands consumer choice for safe dietary supplements by adding a new approved form of magnesium.
policies.environmental_reason: The regulation has no direct impact on environmental protection, pollution, or natural habitats.
policies.economic_reason: Provides a minor economic benefit by opening up a new ingredient option for the health supplement manufacturing industry.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2240 of 5 November 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1442 as regards the transitional measures for plastic materials and articles manufactured with salicylic acid or untreated wood flour or fibres
policies.summary: This regulation gives manufacturers more time to comply with safety rules for certain plastic food packaging made with natural materials like wood flour. It helps businesses avoid supply chain disruptions while ensuring packaging remains safe for consumers. Essentially, it is a routine administrative delay that balances industrial practicality with food safety standards.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by maintaining safety standards while preventing food supply disruptions that could affect consumers.
policies.environmental_reason: Maintains existing environmental standards for plastic materials without creating notable new benefits or harms.
policies.economic_reason: Reduces compliance costs and prevents potential supply chain bottlenecks for manufacturers using bio-based materials.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2224 of 5 November 2025 amending Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Annex II to Directive 2002/46/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards monosodium salt of L-5-methyltetrahydrofolic acid as a source of folic acid added to foods and as a source of folate used in the manufacture of food supplements
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates food safety rules to allow a specific new chemical compound, monosodium salt of L-5-methyltetrahydrofolic acid, to be added to everyday foods and dietary supplements as a source of vitamin B9 (folate). It ensures that this alternative nutrient source meets safety standards and can be legally used by food manufacturers across member states. Ultimately, it gives consumers more choices for getting their essential vitamins through fortified foods and supplements.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to a bioavailable form of folate, which supports public health, particularly for pregnant individuals.
policies.environmental_reason: Has a negligible impact on the environment as it regulates a food additive rather than industrial production or land use.
policies.economic_reason: Provides minor economic benefits to food and supplement manufacturers by legalizing a new ingredient for product development.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2270 of 4 November 2025 establishing a fisheries closure for Norway lobster in area 6; United Kingdom and international waters of 5b for vessels flying the flag of Ireland
policies.summary: This regulation temporarily closes the Norway lobster fishery in specific UK and international waters for Irish fishing vessels. It is an emergency conservation measure implemented to prevent overfishing and help fish populations recover.
policies.social_reason: Restricts the livelihoods and immediate economic security of Irish fishers operating in the affected area.
policies.environmental_reason: Protects marine biodiversity and supports the long-term sustainability of Norway lobster populations by preventing overfishing.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes short-term economic costs and revenue loss for the commercial fishing sector affected by the closure.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2222 of 4 November 2025 refusing to authorise a health claim made on foods and referring to the reduction of disease risk
policies.summary: The European Commission has decided to ban a specific health claim on food products that promised to reduce the risk of a disease. This decision protects consumers from being misled by unproven health benefits on food packaging. It ensures that only scientifically verified health claims can be marketed to the public.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health and consumer rights by preventing misleading disease-reduction claims on food products.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct impact on environmental protection, emissions, or natural habitats.
policies.economic_reason: Promotes fair competition in the food market by ensuring companies cannot gain an unfair advantage through unsubstantiated health claims.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2223 of 4 November 2025 refusing to authorise a health claim made on foods, other than those referring to the reduction of disease risk and to children’s development and health
policies.summary: This European Union regulation bans a specific health claim from being used on food products because it was not scientifically proven. The rule protects consumers from being misled by unverified health benefits on food packaging. Overall, it ensures truth in food marketing without significantly changing the economy or environment.
policies.social_reason: Protects consumers from misleading health claims by ensuring food marketing is scientifically backed.
policies.environmental_reason: The regulation focuses solely on food labeling and has no direct impact on the environment.
policies.economic_reason: Maintains a fair market standard for food labeling without creating significant economic costs or growth.

policies.title: Absent Voting (Elections in Scotland and Wales) Act 2025
policies.summary: This Act makes changes to the rules regarding absent voting, such as postal and proxy voting, specifically for elections in Scotland and Wales. It updates the legal framework governing how citizens can cast their votes without attending a polling station in person.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to the democratic process by refining procedures for postal and proxy voting.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct or significant impact on the natural environment.
policies.economic_reason: Involves administrative updates to voting procedures without a direct effect on economic growth or markets.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2181 of 29 October 2025 amending Regulation (EU) No 142/2011 as regards requirements for the import of used cooking oil
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates the rules and safety requirements for importing used cooking oil from other countries. It aims to ensure that recycled oils brought into the EU meet strict standards to prevent fraud and environmental damage. Ultimately, this helps the EU accurately track and utilize sustainable biofuels derived from waste.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by strengthening import standards for waste oils used in energy production.
policies.environmental_reason: Enhances environmental integrity by preventing fraud in biofuel supply chains and ensuring proper oversight of waste imports.
policies.economic_reason: Promotes fair competition in the green energy market by cracking down on fraudulent or substandard imports.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/2037 of 23 October 2025 amending Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 concerning restrictive measures in respect of actions undermining or threatening the territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence of Ukraine
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates existing restrictive measures and sanctions against individuals and entities that threaten the territorial integrity and independence of Ukraine. policies.title: Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2035 of 23 October 2025 implementing Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 concerning restrictive measures in respect of actions undermining or threatening the territorial integrity, sovereignty and independence of Ukraine
policies.summary: This European Union regulation implements restrictive measures, such as asset freezes and travel bans, against individuals and entities responsible for actions that threaten Ukraine's territorial integrity and sovereignty. policies.economic_reason: Imposes trade restrictions and financial penalties that create minor, targeted market distortions and compliance costs.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/2041 of 23 October 2025 amending Regulation (EC) No 765/2006 concerning restrictive measures in view of the situation in Belarus and the involvement of Belarus in the Russian aggression against Ukraine
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates and tightens existing sanctions against Belarus in response to its involvement in Russia's aggression against Ukraine. It aims to restrict economic activity and resources that support the Belarusian regime and its collaboration in the war. These measures are designed to apply diplomatic and financial pressure to discourage ongoing military cooperation.

policies.title: Canada Gazette - Part II, October 22, 2025, volume 159, number 22

policies.title: Directive (EU) 2025/2205 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 October 2025 on driving licences, amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Directive (EU) 2022/2561 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and repealing Directive 2006/126/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council and Commission Regulation (EU) No 383/2012 (Text with EEA relevance)
policies.summary: This EU directive updates rules on driving licences to make roads safer and modernize the system across member states. policies.title: Directive (EU) 2025/2206 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 October 2025 amending Directive (EU) 2025/2205 as regards certain driving disqualifications
policies.summary: This European Union directive updates rules on driving disqualifications to ensure that serious traffic bans apply across all member countries. It aims to improve road safety by preventing dangerous drivers who lose their license in one country from simply driving in another.

policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct impact on environmental protection, emissions, or natural habitats.
policies.economic_reason: Reduces societal costs associated with traffic accidents and injuries through better enforcement of driving bans.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2084 of 17 October 2025 amending Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the use of quillaia extract (E 999) and Commission Regulation (EU) No 231/2012 as regards the specifications for quillaia extract (E 999)
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates the rules on how quillaia extract, a common food additive, can be used and tested for purity. It ensures that food manufacturers follow updated safety and compositional standards when adding this substance to products.

policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct or significant impact on environmental protection or emissions.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes minor regulatory updates on food businesses with negligible overall impact on market growth or costs.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/2060 of 14 October 2025 amending Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the use of sorbic acid (E 200) and potassium sorbate (E 202) in non-heat-treated plant-based mousses
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates food safety rules to allow the use of specific common preservatives, sorbic acid and potassium sorbate, in plant-based mousses that do not undergo heat treatment. policies.summary: This EU regulation updates and corrects the rules regarding food additives permitted in products designed for particular nutritional uses. It ensures that safety standards and ingredient approvals remain accurate and up-to-date for specialized diets. policies.title: P10_TA(2025)0045 – Common data platform on chemicals, establishing a monitoring and outlook framework for chemicals – Amendments adopted by the European Parliament on 1 April 2025 on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a common data platform on chemicals, laying down rules to ensure that the data contained in it are findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable and establishing a monitoring and outlook framework for chemicals (COM(2023)0779 – C9-0449/2023 – 2023/0453(COD)) (Ordinary legislative procedure: first reading)
policies.summary: This European Parliament regulation establishes a centralized digital platform to collect and share data on chemicals used across the EU. It aims to improve safety tracking, help anticipate future chemical risks, and make information easily accessible to regulators and the public.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health and consumer safety by improving transparency and tracking of hazardous chemicals in everyday products.
policies.environmental_reason: Enhances environmental protection by enabling better monitoring, early warning of chemical pollution, and more informed ecological policymaking.
policies.economic_reason: Improves market efficiency and regulatory clarity for businesses through streamlined data sharing, though it may introduce minor compliance adaptation costs.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/660 of 1 April 2025 amending Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in clay targets
policies.summary: This regulation bans the use of clay targets containing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in shooting sports across the European Union. PAHs are toxic chemical compounds that can accumulate in soil and water around shooting ranges, posing risks to both the environment and human health. The measure aims to phase out these harmful substances to protect ecosystems and prevent toxic contamination.
policies.social_reason: Protects public health by reducing community exposure to carcinogenic and toxic chemical pollutants from shooting ranges.
policies.environmental_reason: Prevents the direct accumulation of hazardous polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in soil and groundwater habitats.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes minor compliance and transition costs on shooting target manufacturers and sports clubs required to switch to safer alternatives.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/639 of 1 April 2025 correcting the Slovenian language version of Annex to Regulation (EU) 2020/354 establishing a list of intended uses of feed intended for particular nutritional purposes
policies.summary: This regulation fixes a translation error in the Slovenian version of an existing European Union rule about animal feed. It ensures that farmers and feed producers in Slovenia have accurate legal text regarding special nutritional animal feeds.
policies.social_reason: Ensures clarity and legal certainty for agricultural workers and animal feed producers in Slovenia.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct impact on environmental protection, conservation, or emissions.
policies.economic_reason: Prevents potential trade confusion and regulatory compliance costs by correcting a linguistic error in agricultural law.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/669 of 31 March 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2025/202 fixing for 2025 and 2026 the fishing opportunities for certain fish stocks, applicable in Union waters and, for Union fishing vessels, in certain non-Union waters
policies.summary: This regulation updates the official catch limits for specific fish stocks for European Union fishing vessels for the years 2025 and 2026. It adjusts quotas to manage marine resources sustainably and comply with international fishing agreements. These periodic updates help balance the needs of the fishing industry with the long-term health of ocean ecosystems.
policies.social_reason: Supports coastal fishing communities and food security by maintaining regulated fishing opportunities.
policies.environmental_reason: Protects marine ecosystems by setting science-based catch limits to prevent overfishing of vulnerable fish stocks.
policies.economic_reason: Provides regulatory certainty and sustainable resource management for the commercial fishing industry over a multi-year period.

policies.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/581 of 27 March 2025 amending Annexes II and IV to Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards maximum residue levels for cycloxydim, dichlorprop-P, flupyradifurone, methyl nonyl ketone, plant oils/citronella oil, potassium sorbate and potassium phosphonate in or on certain products
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates the maximum allowable limits for certain pesticide and chemical residues on food products. It ensures that food sold to consumers remains safe by adjusting safety standards based on the latest scientific evaluations.

policies.environmental_reason: Regulates and potentially limits harmful chemical residues, offering minor benefits to ecological safety.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes standard regulatory adjustments on agricultural trade without significantly driving economic growth or major market costs.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/608 of 24 March 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2022/2309 concerning restrictive measures in view of the situation in Haiti
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates existing sanctions and restrictive measures related to the ongoing crisis and instability in Haiti. It aims to address the deteriorating security situation by tightening or modifying penalties on individuals and entities contributing to the unrest. These measures are designed to support international efforts to restore peace and stability in the region.
policies.social_reason: Supports long-term social stability and human rights in Haiti by targeting destabilizing actors, though the direct domestic impact is indirect.
policies.environmental_reason: The regulation focuses strictly on geopolitical sanctions and security measures, having no direct impact on the environment.
policies.economic_reason: Targeted sanctions on specific individuals and entities have a negligible impact on broader macroeconomic indicators or public-interest economics.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/610 of 24 March 2025 amending Regulation (EU) No 224/2014 concerning restrictive measures in view of the situation in the Central African Republic
policies.summary: This European Union regulation updates financial and travel sanctions related to the ongoing crisis in the Central African Republic. It ensures that restrictive measures remain targeted and aligned with current geopolitical conditions and international security objectives. Overall, it is a foreign policy and security measure with indirect effects on European citizens.
policies.social_reason: Maintains international sanctions and security measures without directly altering the domestic rights, welfare, or health of everyday citizens.
policies.environmental_reason: Focuses strictly on political and financial restrictive measures with no direct impact on environmental protection or pollution.
policies.economic_reason: Imposes targeted financial restrictions on specific entities related to a foreign conflict, resulting in a negligible impact on the broader public economy.

policies.title: Regulation (EU) 2025/535 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 March 2025 establishing the Reform and Growth Facility for the Republic of Moldova
policies.summary: This European Union regulation establishes a financial and reform package to support Moldova's economic growth and preparation for EU membership. It provides targeted funding conditional on the country implementing specific structural, institutional, and anti-corruption reforms. The initiative aims to modernize Moldova's economy, improve public administration, and align its standards closer to the European Union.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to institutional modernization, public services, and better governance standards that improve citizens' overall well-being and rights.
policies.environmental_reason: Promotes sustainable economic development and alignment with European green standards, though environmental goals are secondary to structural reforms.
policies.economic_reason: Boosts economic growth and market integration through targeted financial assistance and mandatory business environment reforms.

policies.summary: This international regulation sets mandatory safety standards for car designs to better protect pedestrians during collisions. It requires vehicles to undergo specific impact tests aimed at reducing head and leg injuries for people walking or cycling. Ultimately, it aims to make roads safer by forcing manufacturers to build more forgiving vehicle fronts.

policies.title: Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 of 11 March 2025 amending Directive 2006/112/EC as regards VAT rules for the digital age
policies.summary: This European Union directive updates tax rules for the digital age to make it easier for businesses to operate online across borders. It modernizes Value Added Tax (VAT) collection, reducing paperwork for companies while helping governments collect taxes more effectively from digital platforms.
policies.social_reason: Expands access to a more harmonized digital single market, indirectly benefiting consumers through streamlined online business operations.
policies.environmental_reason: Neutral regarding environmental impact as it primarily addresses administrative and digital taxation rules.
policies.economic_reason: Benefits the economy by reducing administrative burdens and compliance costs for cross-border digital businesses while closing tax loopholes.

policies.title: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/517 of 11 March 2025 amending Regulation (EU) No 904/2010 as regards the VAT administrative cooperation arrangements needed for the digital age
policies.summary: This EU regulation updates administrative cooperation rules for Value Added Tax (VAT) to adapt tax collection for the digital age, particularly regarding e-commerce and digital platforms. It helps member states better track and collect taxes on online transactions, reducing fraud and administrative burdens. For everyday citizens, it largely operates behind the scenes to ensure a fairer, more digitized tax system without directly changing their tax rates.
policies.social_reason: Supports public services by helping governments efficiently collect tax revenue needed for social welfare and infrastructure.
policies.environmental_reason: Has no direct or significant impact on environmental protection or emissions.
policies.economic_reason: Reduces bureaucratic friction for digital businesses and levels the playing field against tax evasion in e-commerce.
